intro: Watch how the binder affects the paint. Wax can catch light in translucent layers, while paint mixed with milk protein or glue can dry to a flat surface.
alt: Four portraits with translucent wax, opaque casein, chalky distemper and worn blue and red paint on plaster.

variants.name: encaustic
variants.look: Yellow wax catches light over cloudy blue-green layers.
variants.history: Wax-bound paint was used on some Roman Egyptian mummy portraits, where the modeling of a face can still look remarkably fresh.
variants.when: Paint a face or surface with translucent layers and visible depth.
variants.why: Wax can hold both clear glazes and opaque deposits that catch the light differently.

variants.name: casein painting
variants.look: Crisp, flat shapes sit in an opaque, muted palette.
variants.history: Casein is a milk protein historically used as a paint binder. It dries to a matte surface and has been used for murals and commercial art.
variants.when: Paint a study with crisp edges that you will view under bright light.
variants.why: The relatively matte surface reduces glare and gives color shapes a clean edge.

variants.name: distemper
variants.look: Earth colors read as dry, powdery planes.
variants.history: Distemper generally uses a water-based binder such as animal glue with pigment, often with chalk. It appears in historical interiors and on theatrical scenery.
variants.when: Block in broad matte areas for a backdrop or decorative wall.
variants.why: Its flat color keeps reflected light from breaking up the design.

variants.name: fresco secco
variants.look: Blue and red color catches on worn patches of a dry cream wall.
variants.history: Fresco secco applies paint to dried plaster. Painters have used it both on its own and to add detail to frescoes executed on wet plaster.
variants.when: Add details to a wall painting after the plaster has set.
variants.why: The dry surface gives the painter time for finishing touches in specific areas.

prompt: Create one square atlas comparison plate, precisely four independently composed equally sized artwork squares in full-bleed 2x2 grid, hard splits on both midlines, no margin nor gutter. Same waist-up figure and mug at a minimal desk. Use the attached illustration only as subject character reference. 30-year-old attractive ash-blonde woman with tidy low bun, black rectangular eyeglasses clearly visible in every panel, tailored charcoal knee-length business dress under fitted blazer, signature white coffee mug with small four-color windowpane mark and plain blue lanyard with a blank badge. Never reproduce the card border or typography. The artwork techniques differ dramatically. Put nothing that crosses the splits. No letters, words, numerals or panel labels anywhere. TOP LEFT: thick encaustic, honey-colored translucent wax strata and cloudy blue-green highlights. TOP RIGHT: casein painting on board, flat dry milk-paint matte opacity in muted coral and olive, sharp shapes. BOTTOM LEFT: chalky earth-toned distemper painting, powdery flat maroon, ochre, sage and deliberately simple design. BOTTOM RIGHT: fresco secco, figure on dried mottled wall with cream plaster, dusty blue and red appearing rubbed away at edges.
